set.body:
TESTED END TO END against a real neuroim2 mask - 8x8x4 volume, 120 active voxels, spacing 3x3x4, neuroim2 0.19.0 installed. The engine works: neuroim2_volume_domain, neuroim2_searchlights, relation, geometry and contrast all succeeded, producing 120 measurements over searchlights of mean support 11.1. The DISCONTINUITIES ARE AT BOTH ENDS OF THE JOURNEY, and a user hits them in sequence.

DISCONTINUITY 1 - THE FRAME CONSTRUCTORS RETURN DIFFERENT KINDS OF THING.

  searchlights(6)                              -> effect_frame_spec   needs compile_frame()
  neuroim2_searchlights(mask, 6, domain)       -> effect_frame        ALREADY compiled

Every vignette and README example teaches the pattern compile_frame(searchlights(r), domain). A user moving to real data writes the analogous line and gets:

  compile_frame(neuroim2_searchlights(mask, 6, dom), dom)
    -> `specification` must be a valid additive frame specification.

The correct call is to pass the result directly as at=, but nothing says so. The message names what the argument must be and not what was supplied, which is the same defect class as bd-01KZYM1W0WAWVX5MY4T35VYCQH. The asymmetry may well be deliberate - the neuroim2 helper has the mask so it can compile immediately - but it is undocumented, and it breaks the one pattern the documentation drills.

DISCONTINUITY 2 - as_neurovol() REJECTS EVERY VIEW THE PACKAGE PRODUCES.

  as_neurovol(contrast_view, mask)     -> `values` must provide one finite number per
                                          compact domain feature.
  as_neurovol(rdm_view, mask)          -> same
  as_neurovol(contrast_view$total, mask) -> OK, DenseNeuroVol

The signature is as_neurovol(values, mask, domain, fill, label): the first argument is a bare numeric vector. So the user must know to reach inside the view and pull out $total, or $signed, or $coherent, before they can make a map.

This is the step README:379-381 advertises as the way to get results back into brain space, and bd-01KZYARD5697TRN2Q3S0E153BM already records that it is demonstrated nowhere. Now it is clear that a demonstration would not be optional polish: without one, a user cannot guess the call, because every object they are holding is refused and the error talks about finite numbers per feature rather than about the object they passed.

It also interacts badly with the multi-column views. An rdm view has one column per condition pair; there is no single vector to extract, so a user wanting per-pair maps must work out the column structure themselves. No method covers that case.

WHY THESE TWO TOGETHER. Individually each is small. In sequence they bracket the entire real-data journey: the first blocks the user going IN with a real mask, the second blocks them coming OUT with a map. Between them the engine works perfectly. So the path a real fMRI researcher takes is broken at both ends and sound in the middle - which is a compact statement of this whole review.

FIXES:
  1. accept a compiled frame in compile_frame() and return it unchanged, or make the error
     say 'this is already a compiled frame; pass it directly as at='
  2. give as_neurovol() methods for the view classes, defaulting to the natural column
     (total for a contrast view) and erroring informatively for multi-column views, or
     accepting a column name
  3. one worked example carrying mask -> domain -> searchlights -> geometry -> contrast ->
     NeuroVol, which is the vignette bd-01KZYARD5697TRN2Q3S0E153BM asks for and would have
     caught both of these
set.title: The real-data round trip has two undocumented discontinuities on the neuroim2 path
